# Macchajātaka (Ja 216)
**ID:** Ja 216
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Macchajātaka* (Ja 216) is a canonical birth story preserved in the *Dukanipāta* of the Pali *Jātaka* collection [Fausböll 1879; SuttaCentral]. Set at Jetavana, the frame story relates that the Buddha addressed a monk who had grown discontented and lovesick owing to longing for his former wife (*purāṇadutiyikā*) [Fausböll 1879; SuttaCentral]. Warning the monk that this woman had caused him harm in past lives and nearly brought him to being roasted on coals before wise men intervened, the Buddha recounted a tale of the past opening with the verse beginning *Na mayaṁ aggi tapati* ("'Tis not the fire that burns me") [Fausböll 1879; SuttaCentral]. In the past narrative, a fish caught in a net laments not the threat of the cooking fire, but the thought that his female companion will think he deserted her for another; the Bodhisatta, then serving as a royal chaplain (*purohita*), hears the fish's laments by the riverbank and persuades the fishermen (*kevattena*) to release it [Fausböll 1879]. Following the exposition of the four noble truths, the lovesick monk attained stream-entry (*sotāpatti*), and the Buddha revealed the birth identification (*samodhāna*): the female fish was the former wife, the male fish was the lovesick monk, and the Bodhisatta was the chaplain [Fausböll 1879].
This narrative is distinct from homonymous Jātakas sharing the title *Macchajātaka*, notably Ja 34 (which shares a similar frame story but opens with *Na maṁ sītaṁ*) and the well-known rain-making tale Ja 75 (in which the Bodhisatta himself is reborn as the king of fish) [Fausböll 1877; Harris 2009]. SuttaCentral records four modern translations across four languages [SuttaCentral]. No curated external parallels are listed on SuttaCentral, and DharmaNexus records no Pali-internal text reuse or cross-language matches above threshold for this text [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
